host: local CPU-first developer host, single maintainer, no GPU

s21d1_050_frozen_queries.query_text: the failed side's canonical search text, so a query describes a failing state and never its own repair
s21d1_050_frozen_queries.group_exclusion: every query excludes its own group, always
s21d1_050_frozen_queries.why_all_unseen: group identity is one-to-one with task identity in this corpus: 30 coding groups for 30 tasks and one group per fresh case. Excluding the query's group therefore always removes its own task, so the whole benchmark is an unseen-task benchmark by construction rather than by sampling.

relevance_model.tier_1: same task family for coding, same problem type for a fresh pair that has one; 66 queries
relevance_model.tier_2: same domain, used only for the 14 fresh queries whose problem type is unique in the selection; a weaker judgment, reported separately and never blended into a single number
relevance_model.note: Tier 2 exists because the W3b selection maximised problem-type coverage, which left 14 of the 20 fresh cases without a same-type partner. Reporting the tiers apart is the honest handling; merging them would flatter the arms.

graph_arm_versus_strongest_simpler_arm.reading: The graph arm finds a relevant pair inside the top five more often, but orders the whole top ten slightly worse. It wins on whether something useful is present and loses on how well the list is ordered. That is a mixed result and is reported as one; no single metric is selected to make it look decisive.

s21d1_054_results.exact_signature_returns_nothing: correct, not a defect. A signature match requires a candidate sharing the query's task signature, and the query's own group is always excluded, so no such candidate can exist. The arm is precise where it fires and silent everywhere else.

usefulness_floor.verdict: NOT MET. Gate D1 condition 15 stays open.
usefulness_floor.action_taken: reported, not tuned. The pre-registration stop rule is explicit: if no bounded arm reaches the floor, the result is reported and FGW is rejected; the floor is not lowered.
usefulness_floor.honest_caveat: The floor is measured against a cross-task relevance judgment on a benchmark that is entirely unseen-task by construction. That is a harder task than same-task retrieval, and it is the task the Experience Memory Graph exists for. It is context for the number, not a reason to discount it.

defects_found_and_fixed.subject: the vector arm ignored the provider's batch maximum
defects_found_and_fixed.observed: embed_documents refuses a batch above 64 and the eligible pool is 78 candidates, so the arm raised on the first real query.
defects_found_and_fixed.fixed: chunked inside the arm rather than in the caller, because the limit is the provider's and every caller would otherwise hit it.

defects_found_and_fixed.subject: the total query budget was never enforced
defects_found_and_fixed.observed: Only the per-pair GED timeout existed. Ten shortlist entries at 250 ms each already exceed the 2-second budget before any embedding, and the first benchmark measured a p95 of 3523 ms against a 2000 ms bound.
defects_found_and_fixed.fixed: the arm now checks the remaining budget before each comparison and records a cutoff as an explicit bounded result, exactly as section 4.7 requires of a timeout.

defects_found_and_fixed.subject: the budget could still be overshot by a full per-pair timeout
defects_found_and_fixed.observed: Checking only elapsed time let a comparison start at 1999 ms and run its full 250 ms, so p95 measured 2040 ms against a 2000 ms bound.
defects_found_and_fixed.fixed: the check reserves the per-pair timeout, so no comparison can start unless it can also finish inside the budget. p95 fell to 1789 ms.

defects_found_and_fixed.subject: every query re-embedded the whole candidate pool
defects_found_and_fixed.observed: Roughly 936 ms of the graph arm's 940 ms median was re-embedding 78 unchanged candidate texts.
defects_found_and_fixed.fixed: a caller-owned embedding cache. The graph arm's median fell from 940 ms to 25 ms and the vector arm's from 936 ms to 15 ms. This removes waste; it does not change any ranking, and repeated-ranking agreement stayed true across the change.

gate_contribution.condition_14: met: all five arms ran on the same frozen queries, the same pool and the same group exclusions
gate_contribution.condition_15: OPEN: no bounded arm reaches 0.70 top-5 recall or 0.50 MRR@10
gate_contribution.condition_16: met: the graph arm is reported against the strongest simpler arm on every metric including the one it loses, with deterministic ranking and explicit cutoff counts
gate_contribution.condition_17: met: p95 1789 ms inside the 2-second budget, no per-pair comparison exceeded 250 ms, at most 10 results returned
